label: <DEL> step of long (L>=8) sequences, esp. when first token is c/d/n/v/w/f/q/u/a/1/o/l
explanation: Fires almost only at the start of the copy phase. 84% of activation mass is at the <DEL> step (recall_idx 0) and 14% at the next step (recall_idx 1, which outputs orig(1)). It never fires during the original phase. Rate rises steeply with sequence length: the <DEL> step fires 10% of the time overall but ~29% for L>=8 and ~38% for L=9, and L>=8 holds 93% of the mass. Within long sequences the identity of the first token (the token about to be output) modulates firing in a graded way. First tokens c (strongest), d, n, v, w, f, q, u, a, 1, o, l raise the rate; other first tokens rarely fire. The top activations are mostly sequences starting with c, and many contain a g in the middle. The simple rule (phase==1)&(L>=8) gets mass recall 0.80 but precision 0.29 on dev. Adding the first-token set raises precision to 0.54 (F1 0.55, mass recall 0.67 on dev). The remaining dependence looks distributed over sequence content and is not captured by a clean rule.
